items.entity: Side length of the square design domain
items.description: Results, 'Compliance minimization': the text only says 'a square domain is divided evenly by a 4×4 mesh'. It gives no side length or units. The objective is normalized as Ẽ = E/E(ρ_O), so the side length only changes absolute compliance values.
readings: L = 1 (unit square, element size 0.25)
L = 4 (unit-size elements of the 4×4 mesh)

items.description: No thickness is given for this 2D elasticity model. COMSOL's 2D Solid Mechanics default is 1 m.
readings: t = 1 (unit thickness / COMSOL default 1 m)
t = 0.01 (thin plate)

items.entity: Downward force at the 'top right edge'
items.description: Results: 'A force downward is applied at the top right edge' ('As shown in Fig. 2a'). 'Top right edge' is not one of the square's four edges. It could mean the top-right corner (mid-span of the mirrored half-MBB beam next to the symmetry line), the right end of the top boundary, or the top end of the right (symmetry) boundary.
readings: At the top-right corner node (x = L, y = L)
On the top boundary next to the right corner (y = L, x/L in [0.75, 1])
On the upper part of the right/symmetry boundary (x = L, y/L in [0.75, 1])

items.entity: Downward force at top right: point vs. distributed
items.description: Same sentence in Results. The word 'edge' suggests a distributed load, but 'minimizing compliance or the vertical displacement where the external force is applied' suggests a single point load. Whether it is a point or line load, and the loaded length, are shown only in Fig. 2a.
readings: Concentrated point force at one node
Uniform line load over one element edge (length 0.25L, e.g. x/L in [0.75, 1])
Uniform line load over a sub-element segment at the corner (e.g. x/L in [0.9, 1])
Uniform line load over the right half of the top edge (x/L in [0.5, 1])

items.description: No force magnitude or units are given anywhere. The magnitude cancels in the normalized energy Ẽ = E(ρ)/E(ρ_O).
readings: Total force F = 1 (unit)
Unit traction (force per unit length) over the loaded segment
F = 1 kN

items.entity: Roller support at the 'bottom left edge'
items.description: Results: 'the bottom left edge is set as a roller (no vertical displacement)'. The support type (u_y = 0 only) is clear. It is not clear whether the roller is a single corner node or a boundary segment, how long the segment is, or which side it is on. Only Fig. 2a would show this.
readings: Single node at the bottom-left corner (x = 0, y = 0), u_y = 0
Bottom boundary of the bottom-left element, x/L in [0, 0.25], u_y = 0
Short segment at the corner, x/L in [0, 0.1], u_y = 0
Lower part of the left edge, x = 0, y/L in [0, 0.25], u_y = 0

items.entity: Weights w of the volume constraint w·ρ ≤ 0.5
items.description: Eq. (5) says w is 'the vector of linear Gaussian quadrature', and Methods calls the constraint a 'weighted average' using the 'weight of linear Gaussian quadrature'. This is not a standard term and no weights are listed, so it is unclear whether boundary and corner nodes count less. This matters when mapping the constraint to an element-density solver.
readings: Exact integral of the bilinear interpolant divided by the area (trapezoidal weights): corner nodes 1/64, edge nodes 1/32, interior nodes 1/16
Equal weights of 1/25 (plain average of the 25 nodal values)

items.description: Eq. (6) uses Y0, but no value is given.
readings: Y0 = 1 (normalized)
Y0 = 200 GPa (structural steel)
Y0 = 70 GPa (aluminium)

items.description: Poisson's ratio is not given anywhere for the compliance examples.

items.entity: Void/minimum stiffness ε in the SIMP law (Eq. 6)
items.description: Eq. (6) only says 'ε is a small number to avoid numerical singularity'. No value is given. ε is written as an absolute modulus, so the ratio ε/Y0 also depends on the unknown Y0.

items.entity: 2D elasticity assumption (plane stress vs. plane strain)
items.description: The text does not say whether the model is plane stress or plane strain. The FEM was run in COMSOL 5.4, whose 2D Solid Mechanics default is plane strain. Plane strain changes the effective Poisson's ratio (nu becomes nu/(1−nu)).
readings: Plane stress
Plane strain (COMSOL 2D default)

items.entity: Finite element type/order on the 4×4 mesh
items.description: Methods says the FEM was done in COMSOL 5.4 and that 'the meshes of FEM are the same as the design variables', i.e. 4×4 quadrilaterals. The order of the displacement shape functions is not stated. On such a coarse mesh, linear and quadratic elements give quite different stiffness.
readings: 4-node bilinear quadrilateral (Q4)
8-node quadratic serendipity (COMSOL Solid Mechanics default)
9-node biquadratic Lagrange

items.entity: Stiffness evaluation with nodal densities interpolated inside elements
items.description: Eq. (6) applies SIMP pointwise to ρ(x), which is bilinearly interpolated (Eq. 17) from the 25 nodal design variables, so the modulus varies inside each element. The quadrature rule is not given. An element-density structured-grid solver needs an explicit choice of how to map nodal values to element stiffness.
readings: SIMP evaluated at the 2×2 Gauss points of each element from the interpolated density
Higher-order quadrature (3×3 Gauss, or COMSOL's default order for quadratic elements)
Element-constant density: average the 4 nodal values and apply SIMP once per element

items.description: No filter or projection is mentioned for the compliance problems or their MMA benchmark (Fig. 2d). A Helmholtz filter is described in Methods only for the heat-problem 'Approximated' baseline. The design is continuous, with grey densities allowed.
readings: No filter (only the implicit smoothing from bilinear interpolation)
Density filter with rmin = 1.5 element widths
Helmholtz/PDE filter with radius equal to half the design-variable spacing (0.125L), copying the heat-problem baseline

items.entity: Initial design for the gradient-based (MMA) benchmark
items.description: Results/Methods give the benchmark in Fig. 2d (Ẽ = 0.293) as MMA in COMSOL, but do not state the starting design. SIMP with p = 3 is non-convex.
readings: Uniform ρ = 0.5 (same as ρ_O and the volume bound)
Uniform ρ = 1 (upper bound, infeasible start)
Random feasible nodal densities

items.description: Methods only says 'MMA via COMSOL with optimality tolerance as 0.001'. Move limits, asymptote settings and the iteration cap are not given. It is also unclear how COMSOL's optimality tolerance maps to the stopping test of a typical structured-grid code.
readings: COMSOL MMA defaults, stop at optimality tolerance 1e-3
Standard MMA with move limit 0.5, stop when max |Δρ| < 1e-3
Move limit 0.2, stop when relative objective change < 1e-3
